Romeo Doubs O 35.5 Rec Yards (-114)

Big fan of Doubs in Week 1, who should take on a more full-time role as the number two wideout on this New England offense. Obviously, everyone knows about the Pats' addition of AJ Brown this offseason, but Doubs' arrival has gone a little under the radar.

Doubs should be a lock in most 2 WR sets, which is great from a volume perspective, especially for a Patriots team looking to operate even more out of heavy personnel this season. The Seahawks put BTA on the Pats in the Super Bowl, which led New England to run 11 personnel on over 79% of snaps, a 31% jump from their regular-season rate (Per Fantasy Points). 

OC McDaniel's had this to say when asked about his offensive philosophy/personell usage in the Super Bowl during a recent presser: “Yeah, I mean, we never want to go in there and be predictable. I think the score really led to what we ended up doing in the game more than anything else."

I still believe the Pats will struggle to find a rhythm in the run game vs. this Seattle front. Last season, Seattle allowed the league's lowest EPA/Rush. Additionally, TreVeyon Henderson was just ruled out. That leaves Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner as the only healthy RBs on the depth chart. Under Josh McDaniels in 2025, New England already posted a top-6 PROE.

Seattle's secondary may be the only area of "weakness" for this team entering Week 1. Nick Emmanwori is a true question mark, and fellow safety Ty Okada did not participate in Monday's practice.

Last season, the Seahawks deployed 2-high coverage at the league's 6th-highest rate. Doubs, in a highly competitive Packers WR room, led the group with a 23% TPRR vs the coverage last season, among Green Bay WRs with 100+ routes vs the coverage. Seattle also ran the 8th-most zone coverage last season. Doubs ranked 13th among all WRs with 200+ routes against zone in Separation score, while posting the 5th-highest win rate (Per Fantasy Points).
